value.title: ddocs-scan — first-class scanning of deterministic documents
value.summary: flowspace3 indexes *.dd.json natively: one chunk per id-bearing row, cited by dd's own address, with typed edges and an inverse source-file index.

sections.name: summary
sections.value:
Today a deterministic document is invisible to flowspace3. `.dd.json` classifies as a config format and is skipped by discovery (crates/parsers/src/discovery.rs:720); its generated `.dd.md` sibling IS indexed, as one flat heading tree, so the only ddoc content in the index is the lossy projection that can be arbitrarily stale with nothing in-file saying so. Every meaning-shaped question about plans, tasks, acceptance criteria, backpressure rows and findings therefore fails or answers from stale markdown.

This plan makes the row the chunk. A `*.dd.json` is parsed by a pure Rust function into an element tree whose leaves are the id-bearing rows — `ac-`, `tk-`, `dw-`, `bp-`, `lg-`, `fn-`, `fd-`, `vd-`, `ph-` — each keyed on (file, section, id), each carrying its parent trail, its schema, its typed state, and each cited with dd's native address `file#section/id` so `ddocs get` resolves what flowspace3 returns. Typed edges, gate-terminal semantics and derived state come from shelling out to `ddocs --json`, in the imperative shell only, and degrade to "rows indexed, edges absent" when the binary is missing.

The asymmetry that makes this worth doing: dd holds the document side of the graph and answers it forward-only; flowspace3 already holds the code side. The inverse index — given a source file, the ddoc rows that reference it — is a join neither tool can make alone. dd PR #12 (ddoc → ordinary-file edges, `kind: "file"`) is OPEN and NOT MERGED as of 2026-08-28; this plan designs the schema to receive those edges without designing against their absence.

Contract answers measured by dd o-prime (pij-mental-dajeil) against dd main a53b79d on 2026-08-28, and binding on this plan: rows do NOT nest inside rows — the shape is section → (optional dynamic-key map) → row, so the walker recurses STRUCTURALLY and treats any object carrying a string `id` as a row, without assuming a depth. Prose-ness is DECLARED by the schema's shape type, never inferred from a field name: `text` is the prose type, `string` is the catch-all that still carries prose, and `state`/`enum`/`int`/`number`/`bool`/`link`/ids are metadata that dilute the vector. `ddocs --json links <path>` walks the WHOLE corpus per call (measured: scanned 111 to answer about one file), so edges come from one corpus-level `ddocs --json graph`, sliced by us, never from a per-file call on the watcher path. Ids are document-unique but the address grammar is positional, so `file#id` does NOT resolve (measured: E450) and the short citation form is never emitted. `dd.sweep_exclude` means index normally and exclude only from corpus health reporting.

**Where the evidence for this plan's claims lives.** Every claim below is backed by an artefact committed in this repository, because a claim that lives only in a seat's transcript does not survive that seat standing down — a defect the reviewer caught in this plan's own bookkeeping:

- `assets/done-reports.md` — every coder's NAMED mutations verbatim (u1 ten, u3 twelve plus a follow-up, u2 nineteen, u4 eleven), each seat's exact sealed-gate command line, and the toolchain each independently OBSERVED. This is what backs any statement that a test was mutation-checked.
- `assets/integration-proof.md` — the live run on this repo's own ddoc corpus with the branch-built binary: 529 rows from 36 `.dd.json`, zero `.dd.md`, the reorder proof measured on the embeddings table, and both halves of the degradation proof.
- `assets/observations.md` — 29 observations from five seats, rescued verbatim before any worktree was tidied, never cleared.
- `assets/tasks/phase-1/tasks.dd.json` — every task's `done_when` row carries a receipt naming a file:line or the mutation that defends it.
- `assets/brief-ddocs-scan.md` — the domain brief this plan was built from.

The `harness checks` verdicts referenced in this plan were taken on the composed branch with sealed inputs (a private pre-minted database, an isolated `FS3_CONFIG_DIR`, and the pinned toolchain reported as observed rather than assumed).

sections.name: goals
value: Index the source, never the projection: `*.dd.json` is admitted by discovery and parsed; the generated `*.dd.md` sibling is skipped, so a ddoc appears in the index exactly once and never from stale markdown.
Make the ROW the retrievable unit, keyed on (file, section, id), so "which acceptance criterion covers X" returns the criterion — not the plan that contains it.
Cite with dd's own address (`file#section/id`) so any hit flowspace3 returns can be pasted straight into `ddocs get`, and make `flowspace3 get` accept that address form.
Carry the row's meaning as typed, filterable metadata — schema, section, id kind, state, gate-terminal membership, parent trail — rather than burying it in embedded prose.
Walk dd's typed link graph from ONE corpus-level `ddocs --json graph`, slicing edges onto the rows that own them, and never reimplement dd's link resolver or schema resolution.
Serve the inverse index — given a source file path, the ddoc rows referencing it — as the join dd asked us for, built to receive `kind: "file"` edges the day PR #12 lands.
Degrade honestly: with no `ddocs` binary on PATH, rows still index and search still works; only edges and gate semantics go missing, and the envelope says so.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Reimplementing dd's schema resolution, link resolution, or validation in Rust. dd's own guidance is that a Rust parser is a fine second step and a bad first one; schema semantics are exactly where a reimplementation silently diverges.
Writing to ddocs. flowspace3 reads the corpus; it never calls `ddocs set/add/rm` and never edits a `.dd.json` or a `.dd.md`.
Indexing `.dd.md` files as documents in their own right. They are generated, lossy, and can be silently stale.
Treating a validation failure as "not a ddoc". A document with a broken link is still indexed; the finding rides as metadata.
Shipping the `kind: "file"` edge behaviour as a proven feature. PR #12 is open; we build the receiving schema and prove it against a recorded fixture, not against dd main.
A new port trait for ddocs. The architecture's rule 3 stands — a trait earns its existence only when a second real implementation exists; a subprocess call in the imperative shell does not qualify.
Ranking or relevance tuning of ddoc rows against code. Eval fixtures land as evidence; tuning is a later plan.

value.claim: A `*.dd.json` in an indexed root is discovered and parsed: `flowspace3 search` returns individual ROWS from it, and the generated `*.dd.md` sibling contributes no hits. Proven on this repo's own corpus (docs/plans/**, .harness/government/settings.dd.json) as a live fixture.

The row walker recurses a section's value STRUCTURALLY and treats any object carrying a string `id` as a row, so both the plain `section → row` shape and the dynamic-key-map shape (`done_when` → task id → assertion rows) produce rows, each carrying its full parent trail. Rows are not assumed to nest inside rows, and no depth is hardcoded.

Every indexed ddoc row carries dd's native address as its citation in the positional `file#section/id` form, and `flowspace3 get "<file>#<section>/<id>"` resolves the same row `ddocs get` resolves. The short `file#id` form is never emitted, because the grammar is positional and it does not resolve.
Chunk identity is (file, section, id): reordering rows inside a `.dd.json` re-parses the file but causes ZERO new embeddings, proven by an embedding-count assertion across a reorder.

Embedded text for a row is chosen by the SCHEMA's declared shape type — `text` fields embedded, `string` fields embedded and weighted lower, and `state`/`enum`/`int`/`number`/`bool`/`link`/id fields never embedded — and prose-ness is never inferred from a field name. With no resolvable schema the parser degrades to a documented JSON-string-typed fallback and says so in the row's metadata.

A ddoc row hit carries typed metadata — schema, section, id, id kind, state, gate-terminal membership, parent trail — and search can filter on id kind and on gate-open/closed, not on the literal string "unchecked".
Gate-terminal membership is read from the row's schema, never hardcoded to the five built-in completion states; a schema declaring its own vocabulary is honoured.

The derived state is computed behind exactly ONE function whose rule is dd's: collect state entries structurally, incomplete = ids whose state is outside the gate-terminal set, complete = incomplete empty. Where a row's stored `state` disagrees with the derived value, search reports the DERIVED value and returns the stored one explicitly labelled as stored. A fixture in which the two deliberately disagree proves it.

Typed link edges come from ONE corpus-level `ddocs --json graph` invocation, sliced onto the rows that own them with rel, target address and location; a per-file `ddocs --json links` call is never made on the scan or watcher path, because it walks the whole corpus per call. Unknown rels are walked as first-class links rather than dropped.
Corpus health is read from `ddocs --json validate`, never inferred from an empty `issues` list on a `graph`/`links` envelope — dd fails open, and a malformed address returns `ok` with no issues.

The inverse index answers "which ddoc rows reference this source file" from a repo-relative path, and returns an empty, non-erroring result on a corpus with no file edges — correct before dd PR #12 lands and correct after.

The derived half is stamped with the `version` reported by `ddocs --json version` (0.1.0 as measured 2026-08-28), so a dd upgrade re-derives cleanly; the per-verb data payload is parsed defensively, because dd states the envelope is frozen and the payload is not.
value.note: OPEN — ruled by the cross-model reviewer, 2026-08-28, and the PM's proposed 'closed in code / open in system' was explicitly REJECTED as useful diagnosis rather than closure. The stamp is durable and compared correctly, and the recovery path is correct once invoked, but DL-008 means no unchanged file is ever PRESENTED to the comparison: roots.rs enqueues on blob change alone. So ac-000c's promise - a dd upgrade re-derives cleanly - does not hold on a real corpus, and remove+add is the only current trigger. NAMED DEPENDENCY, ruled by o-prime 2026-08-28 and now CITABLE: the parser-version half of the trigger ships in PR #63 (AI-Substrate/flowspace3, w-parser-reindex), which proves A->B stored-row reparse and B->B zero-work and is independently mergeable. The ddoc tooling-version half plus the shared row assertion - one parser-version-only fixture and one tooling-version-only fixture - land as w-parser-reindex-2, dispatched by that packet's owner immediately after 008 merges; its predicate is already shaped to extend additively. Its predicate is being shaped extensible now so the ddoc half is additive. This criterion cites that named dependency rather than an open hope, and CLOSES on that follow-up's recorded run - post-merge closure on evidence beats holding either PR open across the other's review window. The version comparison is ratified as equality-only, never ordered. CLOSURE CONDITION, reviewer's wording: close fn-0004 only when a system-level test starts from an unchanged indexed blob, changes tooling/facts, uses the supported rescan/upgrade path, and observes the row re-parsed and re-derived WITHOUT remove+add.
value.notes: SHIPS UNMET (state=blocked: open, awaiting external work). The PARSER_VERSION half closed on main #63's own tests (blobs_with_parser_version now makes the unchanged test conjunctive over independent generation stamps). The ddocs tooling-version half is NOT closed: tooling_version is still not a member of that conjunction, so upgrading ddocs alone re-presents nothing. Owner: w-parser-reindex-2 (crayfish). Its dispatch trigger FIRED on this merge by the boundary ruling and is HELD under Jordan's drain order - HELD, NOT FORGOTTEN. Closure test: upgrade ddocs alone, rescan, and observe presented rows re-derived without a remove+add.

value.claim: With no `ddocs` binary on PATH the whole pipeline still indexes rows and serves search; only edges, gate semantics and derived state are absent, and the envelope's `next_action` names the missing binary.
value.note: NARROWED at composition, deliberately: the next_action fires for CWD-SCOPED searches only. The tooling snapshot is keyed by worktree_id and a search scope carries an optional root, so scope.worktree -> find_worktree -> id -> ddoc_tooling(id) is attributable; an explicit --repo or all-roots scope may span several worktrees and a failed lookup proves nothing. u4 stays SILENT in both, rather than warn on an unrelated or unprobed root. Accepted because the alternative trains people to ignore the notice, and because the cwd-scoped search is the shape an agent working in a repo actually runs. Limitation recorded rather than hidden.

value.claim: A document declaring `dd.sweep_exclude` is indexed normally and excluded only from corpus health reporting — never made invisible, because a user cannot tell absence from non-existence.
`sections` with no id-bearing rows chunk as the section, and the whole document is never the primary chunk.
A ddoc whose schema does not resolve, or whose links are broken, is still indexed; the finding rides as row metadata rather than suppressing the document.
`harness checks` is green on the composed branch: fmt, clippy -D warnings, all tests, and the architecture allowlist — with any new dependency edge added as one deliberate allowlist line.
`flowspace3 docs get ddocs` returns a bundled page telling an agent what a ddoc row hit means and how to cite it, and the bundled-docs honesty test (crates/cli/tests/docs_bundle.rs) stays green.

Eval fixtures exist for the three query shapes dd named highest-value — "which acceptance criteria are still open", "which tasks claim this criterion", "which criteria touch this source file" — and are recorded as the plan's exit evidence.

value.title: Contracts (wave 0, PM-authored)
value.objective: Freeze the seams every unit codes against, in one commit, before any coder is spawned.
value.brief: The shared core types are authored by the PM on the plan branch so four units compile and test independently from their first minute: the `ElementKind::Row` variant, the additive `Element.ddoc` field, the `DdocMeta`/`DdocRel`/`DdocSchemaFacts` types, the positional dd address parser, and the single derived-state function. Tenet 2 — freeze the seams before you spawn anyone. Tenet 10 — the toolchain is pinned here (cargo 1.95.0, ddocs 0.1.0 / node 24.7.0 as measured 2026-08-28) and no unit may change it; every done receipt carries the versions it actually observed.
value.key_risks: If a unit needs to widen one of these types mid-flight that is a PM ruling, not a coder edit; a silent widening is the contract drift this phase exists to prevent.
value.receipt: Wave 0 landed at f13186b; harness checks green 2026-08-28T05:56:52Z; tk-0001 assertions all checked with receipts.

value.title: Parse and persist (wave 1)
value.objective: Turn a `.dd.json` on disk into stored, embeddable rows.
value.brief: Two units in parallel behind the wave-0 contract: the pure ddoc parser plus discovery admission (crates/parsers), and the persistence layer plus inverse index (crates/store). They share no files; both consume the frozen core types.
value.key_risks: Discovery classifies `.dd.json` as a config format and skips it (crates/parsers/src/discovery.rs:720); admission must be an exact suffix exception placed BEFORE the config exclusion and must apply to the watcher path (crates/daemon/src/watch.rs:275) as well as add-root.
value.receipt: Wave 1 composed on 008-ddocs-scan: u1 d79e9bc + u3 c3dca20 merged; harness checks green on all nine gates (docs, lock, testdb, fmt, clippy -D warnings, prodguard before/after, cargo test --all, arch) 2026-08-28.

value.title: Enrich and surface (wave 2)
value.objective: Attach dd's typed graph, and make the rows answerable to an agent.
value.brief: Two units in parallel: the `ddocs --json` adapter in the imperative shell (one corpus-level graph call, schema facts, gate-terminal, derived state, version stamping, degradation) and the agent-facing surface (search filters, hit metadata, `get` by dd address, bundled doc page, eval fixtures).
value.key_risks: Both units live in crates/daemon; the collision surface is deliberately engineered down to one `pub mod` line each in the daemon's module list.
value.receipt: Wave 2 composed: u2 614bf2e + u4 83cc5ca merged, PM wiring fd470a2, PARSER_VERSION bump 23ed91e. harness checks green 9/9 at 0d4163b.

value.title: Compose, prove, review
value.objective: Wire the four units into one system, prove it end to end, and get it reviewed.
value.brief: PM-owned. Merge unit branches in dependency order, make `harness checks` green on the composed tree, run the named integration proof against this repo's own ddoc corpus, then cross-model review, then the PR into main.
value.key_risks: Composition is wiring, not building: if a unit needs internal rework at compose time that is a defect in the contracts phase, and it gets ruled, not patched over.

value.approach:
Per-crate, matching the architecture's testing table, with every unit proving its contract STANDALONE and offline.

**core (wave 0)** — plain unit tests on pure functions, no doubles: address parse/render round-trip including the positional grammar and the rejected short form; derived-state over gate-terminal sets including a schema with a custom vocabulary; serde round-trip of the ddoc metadata.

**parsers (u1)** — committed fixture corpora under `crates/parsers/fixtures/ddoc/` compared against whole-tree expectations: the plain `section → row` shape, the dynamic-key-map shape (`done_when` → task id → assertion rows), a section with no ids chunking as the section, a document with an unresolvable schema taking the documented fallback, and the reorder fixture — the same document with its rows reversed — asserting identical row addresses and identical content hashes. Discovery tests assert `.dd.json` admitted, `.dd.md` skipped, and ordinary `.json` still skipped.

**store (u3)** — integration against the real dockerized Postgres per req 33: metadata round-trips through upsert and read, the new filters produce the right rows, the inverse index returns empty-not-error on a corpus with no file edges, and the migration applies forward on a database already carrying code elements.

**daemon adapter (u2)** — pure envelope parsing tested against RECORDED `ddocs --json` outputs committed as fixtures, including one graph envelope carrying `kind: "file"` edges that dd main cannot yet produce; the degradation path is tested by pointing the adapter at a binary that does not exist and asserting rows still index.

**surface (u4)** — daemon endpoint tests asserting the new hit fields and filters, and eval fixtures under `eval/` for the three named query shapes.

**Mutation discipline**: every fix-test must be mutation-checked — break the code, watch the named test fail, restore. A test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence.

**Integration proof (PM, at composition)**: this repo's own ddoc corpus indexed end to end, then the three named queries run live and their transcripts captured as the plan's exit evidence.
value.rationale: Every unit must prove its contract standalone and offline, because units are dispatched in parallel and a unit that cannot be judged alone cannot be accepted alone. The architecture already answers how: core needs no doubles, parsers use fixture files, store runs against real dockerized Postgres, and ports use testkit fakes. Nothing here invents a new testing mechanism.
value.focus_areas: The reorder-produces-zero-new-embeddings assertion (the trap dd warned about, and the only direct evidence that chunk identity really is (file, section, id)) · the stored-vs-derived disagreement fixture · the missing-binary degradation path · discovery admitting `.dd.json` while still skipping ordinary `.json` and the generated `.dd.md` · the recorded graph envelope carrying `kind: "file"` edges that dd main cannot yet emit.
value.excluded: Ranking and relevance quality of ddoc rows against code — eval fixtures are recorded as evidence, not asserted as thresholds; tuning is a later plan. Live runs against a real `ddocs` binary are not a CI requirement: CI runs against recorded envelopes, and the live path is exercised in the PM's integration proof.
value.mock_usage: None. Mocking frameworks are refused by name in the architecture. The doubles used are shipped testkit fakes for the two ports, committed fixture files for the parser, and recorded `ddocs --json` envelopes for the adapter — all real inputs, none of them per-test throwaways.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value:
1. dd PR #12 (`kind: "file"` edges) is OPEN, not merged. Designing against its absence would make the inverse index unbuildable later; assuming it landed would make wave 2 untestable. Retired by: the edge schema accepts `kind` as an open string, and the inverse index is proven against a RECORDED envelope fixture containing file edges, not against dd main.

2. The derived-state rule must be implemented in Rust because dd's own `deriveItems`/`deriveState`/`deriveRollup` (src/core/derive.ts) are unreachable — dd o-prime measured that there is no `./core/derive` export and no CLI verb surfaces it. This is exactly the drifting second implementation dd warned against. Retired by: the rule lives behind ONE function so swapping it for a call is a one-line change, gate_terminal is read from the schema rather than hardcoded, and a scoped ask for a `ddocs --json derive` verb is filed with dd naming flowspace3 as the consumer.

3. `ddocs --json links <path>` walks the whole corpus per call — measured by dd o-prime at 111 documents scanned to answer about one file — so the obvious per-file call is quadratic on a watcher. Retired by: edges come from one corpus-level `ddocs --json graph`, sliced by us; a per-file `links` call on the scan path is a review-blocking defect. Residual: no cheap corpus-change detector exists (dd has node shas, no edge-set stamp), so graph refresh is time/generation-based and its cost is measured before wave 2 closes.

4. dd fails OPEN asymmetrically: an unresolvable schema returns degraded WITH an issue, but a malformed address inside a document returns `ok` with an EMPTY issues list. Reading empty issues as healthy would make us silently confident. Retired by: health comes from `ddocs --json validate` only; `graph`/`links` are used for edges and never for health.

5. A row's stored `state` and its derived summary are separate claims dd does not reconcile. Surfacing the stored value as truth would make search confidently wrong about the one number everyone asks for. Retired by: the derived value is what search reports, the stored value is labelled, and a fixture makes the two disagree on purpose.

6. Shelling out to an external binary from the daemon introduces a dependency the architecture has never had. Retired by: the subprocess call is a thin function in the imperative shell, all parsing is pure core functions over recorded envelopes, no new port trait is created (architecture rule 3 stands), and absence of the binary is a tested degradation path rather than an error.

7. The shared global toolchain hazard (tenet 10): four units read one installed `ddocs` and one cargo, so a unit upgrading either invalidates its siblings retroactively and invisibly — they stay green and become wrong. Retired by: cargo 1.95.0 and ddocs 0.1.0/node 24.7.0 are pinned in wave 0, no unit may change them, and every done receipt carries the versions it actually observed.

8. dd states the `--json` ENVELOPE is the contract but the per-verb DATA payload is not frozen, and it moved within the last month (file links added `kind` to edges and `file_findings` to build). Retired by: defensive payload parsing that ignores unknown fields, plus keying re-derivation on the recorded `ddocs --json version`.

9. The elements table's uniqueness is (blob_sha, parser_version, address, span_start), so a row reorder changes span_start and writes new element rows. Retired by: embedding work is keyed on raw_hash content identity, so a reorder must produce ZERO new embeddings — asserted directly, because this is the trap dd warned about and the assertion is the only thing that proves we avoided it.

10. This repo's own corpus is the live fixture, so a change to our own plan documents can move the test. Retired by: unit tests use committed fixtures under crates/parsers/fixtures; the live corpus is used for the integration proof only.

11. ASSUMPTION, unproven until wave 1: that a ddoc row fits the existing `Element`/`elements` pipeline with one additive typed field, rather than needing a parallel table. This is what buys us embedding, search, get and enrichment for free. If it fails, the plan's cost roughly doubles — so it is proven first, in wave 1, not discovered at composition.

---

## Limitations found by cross-model review, recorded rather than fixed

12. DUPLICATE CONTENT AT TWO PATHS BREAKS `get` FOR THAT CONTENT. The element tree is keyed on (blob, parser_version) while one blob can legitimately appear at N paths, and `get_elements` assumes exactly one file root. Measured both ways: identical `a.dd.json` + `nested/b.dd.json` produce one blob with two file roots, and identical `c.rs` + `nested/d.rs` do exactly the same. PRE-EXISTING and not ddoc-specific — but ddocs make it far likelier, because templated plans, copied packets and recorded fixtures duplicate content in a way source files rarely do. Escalated to o-prime for its own owner and packet; fixing it means changing how the store models a tree's identity, which is an architecture change well outside a plan about scanning documents.

13. DUPLICATE-TEXT ROWS COLLAPSE IN SEMANTIC SEARCH. Embedding identity is `raw_hash` and the search join resolves a vector hit to the lowest-id element carrying that hash, so two rows with identical text share one embedding and only one is ever returned. Measured on this repo: 31 raw_hashes are shared across 116 of 531 distinct ddoc row addresses (22%) — for example `packet-coder-u1/u2/u3/u4.dd.json#refs/r5` are four distinct rows with identical text, and semantic search can surface only one of them. This is the direct flip side of the property that makes a reorder free: content-keyed enrichment is what avoids re-embedding, and it is also what collapses genuinely distinct rows. The plan claims one chunk per row, which is true of STORAGE and addressing (all four rows exist and all four resolve by address) but not of semantic retrieval. Not fixed here: the honest fix is a row-owner expansion at the query layer, which is a change to shared search behaviour affecting code elements equally.

14. DERIVED STATE COVERS ASSERTION LISTS ONLY, NOT ROLLUPS ACROSS DOCUMENTS. A phase row carrying `derives` edges to a tasks section gets `derived_state: null`, so its gate answer falls back to the stored claim. Deliberate: computing a rollup across linked documents is exactly the traversal dd is building its `derive` verb for (outbound `derives`, inbound `satisfies`), flowspace3 has committed to consuming that verb and deleting its own port the day it merges, and shipping a second rollup implementation now is the drifting-second-implementation dd explicitly warned against.

15. ac-000c IS OPEN AT SHIP, not closed. The ddocs version is now persisted per row and compared for equality, and the skip path re-enriches and re-parses when tooling or schema facts change — but DL-008 means an unchanged file is never enqueued, so nothing presents it to that comparison. The reviewer rejected the PM's "closed in code / open in system" framing as diagnosis rather than closure, and it was right to: a promise that holds only when a user happens to run remove+add is not a promise the product keeps. Both layers ship named under one open finding, with remove+add stated as the only current trigger.

16. A ROW PARSED UNDER FALLBACK KEEPS ITS FALLBACK VECTOR until re-parsed. Found by the reviewer, and it disproved a claim the PM had repeated all day: a degraded row recovers its METADATA when tooling returns, but `raw_text` and `embed_basis` are produced by the parser alone, so enrichment cannot rebuild the text that search actually ranks on. Fixed by re-parsing on the skip path when schema-facts availability changed — which makes recovery POSSIBLE; risk 15 is why it does not yet happen automatically.

value.question: Should dd export `./core/derive` (or, better for a Rust consumer, surface it as a `ddocs --json derive <address>` verb)? dd o-prime measured that `deriveItems`/`deriveState`/`deriveRollup` exist in src/core/derive.ts but are reachable from neither Node nor the CLI, and offered to put a scoped ask to Jordan if a named consumer exists. flowspace3 is that consumer.
value.note: ANSWERED 2026-08-28: dd is BUILDING the verb. pij-mental-dajeil confirmed and spawned pij-voiceless-porpoise (worktree dd-worktrees/derive-verb) with flowspace3 named as the consumer. Settled payload: data{address, complete, gate_terminal (resolved per node from that node's own schema), total (at every level), incomplete[]{id, address, state, section}, nodes[] (RECURSIVE, never flattened), basis[] (closure of documents consulted - repo-relative, sorted, includes the root; this is our invalidation key), degradations[]{reason, address, detail}}. Deterministic traversal order for nodes and incomplete, so we assert on order rather than sorting. Unreachable descendant => status degraded, nodes named, counted INCOMPLETE, complete=false (dajeil ruling). No input digest in this change. Our commitment: consume it and delete fs3_core::ddoc::derive_state in the same commit.

value.question: Is a cheap corpus-change detector possible, so the corpus-level `ddocs --json graph` is refreshed only when the edge set could have moved? dd has node shas but no edge-set stamp, and dd o-prime declined to invent one, asking to see ours if we build it.
value.note: Wave-2 measurement task. Interim: refresh on a generation counter bumped by any ddoc scan, cost measured before wave 2 closes.

value.question: Coder model discrepancy for prime, not for dd: the domain brief names coders as `gpt-5.6-sol-fast-1m high`, while `.harness/government/settings.dd.md` — Jordan's 2026-08-28 ruling — names coders as `github-copilot/claude-opus-5 high`. This plan follows settings as the newer governance authority.
value.note: Flagged to pij-instant-lynx for a ruling before wave 1 spawns.

value.question: When do flowspace3's ddoc data-shape assumptions freeze? dd o-prime asked to be told, so it knows what a dd change would break.
value.note: Answer: at the end of wave 0 (the contracts commit). To be reported to pij-mental-dajeil with the frozen type definitions.
